rounds.text: Amco India Ltd trades at a steep discount to its net worth with a price-to-book ratio of 0.72x against a sector benchmark of 2.44x [E2, E7]. The business is also available at an EV/EBITDA of 9.32x, sitting comfortably below the sector benchmark of 12.59x [E11]. Recent operational updates reveal a significant turnaround, featuring a TTM compounded sales growth of 15% and a quarterly operating margin expanding to 4% in June 2026 compared to 0% in the year-ago quarter [E17, E31]. These accelerating fundamentals align with a strong macro backdrop, as the Capital Goods sector enjoys a positive tailwind score of 0.67 [E60, E61]. Conceded: [E34], [E41], [E50].

Amco India Ltd trades at a severe valuation disconnect against its actual fundamental delivery, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at ₹27 per share compared to a market price of ₹66, resulting in a staggering negative margin of safety of -146.4% [E41, E42]. The reverse DCF highlights that the current price assumes an unrealistic 12.6% earnings growth when the base case demands 0.0%, meaning substantial unearned optimism is already priced into the stock [E43, E59]. Profitability metrics are exceptionally weak, evidenced by a dismal return on equity of 1.8% and a median 10-year ROE of just 4%, alongside a ROCE of only 3.08% or 4.7% depending on the metric source, lagging far behind the sector benchmark of 12.92% [E9, E10, E12, E13, E26]. Furthermore, reported earnings are inflated by ₹1.50 crore of other income, masking underlying operational weakness [E51], which is corroborated by negative operating and free cash flows of ₹1 crore each in March 2026 [E34, E35]. Compounded sales growth has contracted by 9% over the past three years, and five-year profit growth sits at -14%, compounded by a complete lack of shareholder returns through a 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E4, E16, E19, E48]. Conceded: the company demonstrates recent acceleration with a 15% TTM sales growth and a net profit surge of 771% YoY alongside capital goods sector tailwinds [E17, E55, E60].

Conceded: intrinsic value sits below the market price [E41, E42]. However, dismissing the stock on static DCF metrics ignores active cyclical inflections and sectoral tailwinds [E46, E60]. The bear highlights low historical ROE figures, but completely overlooks that quarterly operating margin has surged by 4 percentage points to 4% in June 2026, and TTM sales growth has accelerated to 15% [E17, E31]. Furthermore, the valuation trades at a steep discount on asset backing with a price-to-book of 0.72x against a sector benchmark of 2.44x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 9.32x compared to the sector's 12.59x [E7, E11]. Promoter holding remains rock-solid and unwavering at 65.55%, demonstrating high insider alignment through the recent operational pivot [E39, E61].

Conceded: quarterly operating margin surged to 4% in June 2026 and TTM sales growth accelerated to 15% [E17, E31]. However, pointing to these short-term metrics ignores the longer-term structural reality of a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -9% and a 5-year profit contraction of -14% [E16, E19]. The bull relies on asset-backing discounts like a 0.72x P/B and a 9.32x EV/EBITDA, but these are offset by deeply depressed profitability with an ROE of 0.87% and an ROCE of 3.08% lagging far behind sector benchmarks [E7, E9, E10, E11]. Conceded: promoter holding is stable at 65.55% [E39], but high insider ownership does not rescue a business generating negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -1 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. Furthermore, leaning on sector tailwinds glosses over the fact that current earnings are artificially propped up by Rs 1.50 Cr of other income rather than core operations [E51, E60]. Finally, while the bull dismisses static DCF models as ignoring cyclical inflections, the reverse DCF confirms that today's price already aggressively prices in 12.6% earnings growth against a baseline of 0.0% [E41, E43, E46].
